shortDescription: Zealand Pharma OMXCOP:ZEAL and Boehringer Ingelheim's experimental obesity drug did not increase the risk of serious heart problems compared to a placebo in a late-stage trial, the companies said on Monday.

children: and Boehringer Ingelheim's experimental obesity drug did not increase the risk of serious heart problems compared to a placebo in a late-stage trial, the companies said on Monday.
The study enrolled 5,530 adults with obesity who had cardiovascular diseases, chronic kidney diseases, or at least two weight-related complications or cardiovascular risk factors
The trial met its main goal by showing that the drug, survodutide, did not increase the risk of major cardiovascular events, including heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death
Patients receiving survodutide lost up to 13.7% of their body weight after 72 weeks and also saw greater reductions in blood pressure and waist circumference than those on placebo, the companies said

Stomach-related side effects were the most common, including nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. About 20% of the patients on survodutide stopped treatment because of these side effects, compared with 1.9% on placebo
Survodutide, a dual glucagon/GLP-1 receptor agonist licensed by Boehringer Ingelheim from Zealand Pharma, is being developed for obesity and related cardiometabolic diseases
Boehringer, which holds global development and commercialization rights for survodutide, plans to submit an application for global regulatory approval to treat obesity
